headline: Lineage genealogies and stochastic dynamics infer selection in clonal hematopoiesis
label: Single Cell Clonal Selection Inference
summary: Recent preprints use single-cell genealogies and diffusion-based stochastic models to read selection from clonal dynamics in hematopoiesis.
synthesis: The common thread is inferring selection from the genealogical and temporal structure of allele or clonal dynamics. In aged murine and human HSCs, single-cell RNA-seq with joint variant filtering reconstructs somatic mutation genealogies and reveals a divergent mutational and clonal landscape that is not linked to aging-associated clonal hematopoiesis. BESTish applies a diffusion-approximation stochastic model with Bayesian inference to estimate fitness, mutation rate, and environmental strength in clonal hematopoiesis. Outside hematopoiesis, a published benchmark evaluates four allele-frequency time-series selection methods on simulated sparse ancient-DNA-like data, and a separate published study modifies STRUCTURE parameterization to reduce sampling and population-size biases in walnut domestication genomics. What is new is the use of lineage genealogy and population-level stochastic dynamics as direct readouts of selection rather than as mean-based endpoints. Only the aDNA benchmark and walnut study are published; the hematopoietic items are preprints.
